skill.name: iterative-runner
skill.description: Run bounded AI coding retry loops for TDD, test fixes, and long tasks. The skill helps define success criteria, iteration limits, and blocker reports.
skill.summary: Guide Claude, Codex, or Claude Code through bounded retry loops until clear completion criteria are met.
skill.author: BarisSozen

content.value_statement: Long coding tasks can stall when tests fail or completion criteria are vague. This skill structures bounded retry loops for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
actual_capabilities: Guides repeat-until-complete workflows for AI coding agents.
Defines success criteria such as passing tests and clean lint results.
Encourages maximum iteration limits to prevent runaway loops.
Provides a TDD loop pattern for test-first implementation.
Includes blocker reporting after repeated failed attempts.
limitations: It does not include an executable iterative-runner program.
It depends on clear prompts and measurable success criteria.
High iteration limits can consume time, tokens, and compute.
It cannot make flaky tests or unstable services deterministic.

use_cases.title: Drive a TDD implementation
use_cases.description: Run a bounded loop that writes tests, implements code, and repeats until the test suite passes.

use_cases.title: Retry a long build task
use_cases.description: Keep an AI agent focused on a complex implementation while requiring clear stop conditions and blocker notes.

use_cases.title: Stabilize failing checks
use_cases.description: Iterate on test and lint failures with a fixed attempt limit and a final summary of remaining problems.

prompt_templates.title: Bounded first run
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner prompt for a small task.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use iterative-runner for this task: [task]. Stop after 10 iterations. Finish only when [success criteria] is true.

prompt_templates.title: Make tests pass
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this when tests already exist.
prompt_templates.prompt: Run a retry loop until all tests pass. After each failure, inspect the cause, make the smallest fix, and test again.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor with checks
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this for controlled code cleanup.
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor [area] without changing behavior. Repeat until tests and lint pass. Stop after 20 iterations and report blockers.

prompt_templates.title: Multi-phase delivery loop
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced prompt for larger implementation work.
prompt_templates.prompt: Complete [feature] in phases: tests, implementation, verification, and cleanup. Continue until all criteria pass or 30 iterations fail.

output_examples.input: Implement account settings with tests and a 20 iteration limit.
output: Defines passing tests and clean lint as completion criteria.
Runs each iteration against the same verification steps.
Stops when checks pass or reports remaining blockers.

output_examples.input: Fix a flaky integration test without changing public behavior.
output: Investigates repeated failure causes before editing.
Applies small fixes and reruns the target checks.
Summarizes unresolved instability when the limit is reached.

output_examples.input: Refactor a module overnight with strict stop criteria.
output: Uses a fixed maximum iteration count.
Requires evidence that tests and lint passed.
Produces a concise blocker report if completion fails.

best_practices: Define observable success criteria before starting the loop.
Set a maximum iteration count for every run.
Require blocker notes after repeated failed attempts.
anti_patterns: Running open-ended loops with no iteration limit.
Using vague completion criteria such as make it better.
Letting the agent make broad changes without tests or review.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It helps structure retry loops for AI coding tasks until clear completion criteria are met.

faq.question: Does it run commands automatically?
faq.answer: The skill file provides instructions and examples. It does not include executable files by itself.

faq.question: How do I avoid infinite loops?
faq.answer: Always set a maximum iteration count and define a clear stop condition before starting.

faq.question: Can I use it with Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: What success criteria work best?
faq.answer: Use measurable checks, such as passing tests, clean lint output, or an explicit completion marker.

faq.question: Can it fix flaky tests?
faq.answer: It can guide repeated investigation and fixes, but it cannot guarantee deterministic external systems.
